title: A compacted topic still shows old records for a key you thought was deleted: why (tombstone retention)?
shortTitle: A compacted topic still shows old records for a key you thought was deleted: why (tombstone retention)?

s1_definition.oneliner: Deletion in a compacted topic is a tombstone, and compaction is a lazy background job that skips the active segment and keeps tombstones for `delete.retention.ms`, so seeing old records for a deleted key right after the delete is expected timing, not a failure.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Tombstone** -- a record with the key you want to delete and a null value; it is how you delete a key in a compacted topic.
- **Log compaction** -- a background process that rewrites closed segments to keep only the latest value per key; it is asynchronous and not instant.
- **Active segment** -- the newest segment being appended to; the log cleaner never touches it, only closed segments.
- **delete.retention.ms** -- how long the tombstone itself is kept (default 24 hours) so consumers have time to read the delete before it vanishes.
- **min.cleanable.dirty.ratio** -- the fraction of the log that must be stale before the cleaner runs on that partition.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India keeps one noticeboard per account where only the latest notice should remain. To cancel Rajesh's standing instruction, a clerk pins a blank cancelled slip. But the tidy-up crew works on a schedule and never touches the last few pinned slips. The rule also says to leave the cancelled slip up for a full day so every branch reads it. If you glance at the board right after pinning, the old instruction is still visible. It is not a bug; the cleanup has not reached that part of the board yet.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
 Compaction and Tombstone Timeline
 ===================================

  t=0: Producer writes SAV2001 = {name: Rajesh, tier: gold}
  t=1: Producer writes SAV2001 = {name: Rajesh, tier: platinum}
  t=2: Producer sends tombstone: SAV2001 = null

  Log state after t=2:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Closed Segment 1 (eligible)          │
  │  offset 0: SAV2001 = {tier: gold}    │
  │  offset 1: SAV2001 = {tier: platinum}│
  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Active Segment 2 (NOT eligible)      │
  │  offset 2: SAV2001 = null (tombstone)│
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  Cleaner has NOT run yet:
    All three records visible to consumer

  After compaction runs on Segment 1:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Compacted Segment 1                  │
  │  (offset 0 and 1 removed)            │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Active Segment 2                     │
  │  offset 2: SAV2001 = null (tombstone)│
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  After delete.retention.ms expires:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Tombstone also removed               │
  │ SAV2001 completely gone               │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
In a compacted topic, deleting a key means publishing a tombstone with a null value. Compaction then promises to keep only the latest value per key and eventually remove old values and the tombstone. The reason you still see old records after sending a tombstone is that compaction is asynchronous, never touches the active segment, and retains the tombstone for delete.retention.ms so slow consumers can read the delete.

Consumers must treat null values as evictions. A consumer that ignores nulls keeps a stale entry forever, even after compaction removes the old records from the log.

In my National Bank of India compliance work, we sent a tombstone for Rajesh's profile and immediately replayed the topic -- three old versions were still visible. The cleaner had not yet run. After compaction the old versions collapsed, and the tombstone stayed for the retention window.

Remember one sentence: compaction is a lazy background job that keeps tombstones for delete.retention.ms, so old records after a delete is expected timing, not a failure -- and consumers must handle null values as evictions.

---

keyPoints: Deletion in a compacted topic means sending a tombstone: a record with the key and a null value.
Compaction is asynchronous and runs in the background; old records are not removed instantly.
The active segment is never compacted; only closed segments are eligible for the log cleaner.
Tombstones are retained for delete.retention.ms (default 24 hours) so slow consumers can read the delete.
Consumers must treat null values as evictions or they will keep stale entries forever.
Null-key records cannot be compacted and linger until ordinary retention removes them.
